articles.title: Scottish Football Podcast - What’s going wrong at Hearts - Injuries, tactics or individual errors? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Why are Hearts conceding so many goals and how do they stop the slide?
articles.body:
Radio Scotland , · 11 Nov 2026 , · 29 mins

Hearts have lost three successive games and conceded 10 goals in the process. So what’s gone wrong at Tynecastle? Martin Dowden is joined by former Hearts defender Ryan McGowan and Hearts Standard editor Joel Sked to assess the problems. How much blame lies with Wouter Vrancken's tactics and how much with individual mistakes? Is the punishing schedule exposing Hearts’ injury crisis? Does Vrancken need a Plan B? Nottingham Forest vs Man City odds and score prediction

There is a very good case for opposing Manchester City. The timing of this fixture plays a huge part.

This particular gameweek, the final one before the November international break, carries a big warning sign for anyone looking to follow the formbook.

For the likes of Manchester City, this is their ninth game in the last month. That comes on the back of an exhausting international break in which plenty of players were asked to play four times in 10 days. Eventually, the pressure valve has to hit the red zone. Fatigue creeps in, sharpness drops and performances can suffer.

History suggests this is a gameweek when strange results are more likely than the market expects. City themselves lost 2-1 at home to Brentford in 2022/23, when the Bees were 20/1. Chelsea were held at home by Burnley in 2021/22 despite being priced at 1/7 to win, while Ipswich beat Tottenham at 8/1 in 2024/25 and Sunderland drew 2-2 with Arsenal last season when they were 1/3.

The numbers back up the theory. Blindly backing every odds-on favourite in this particular pre-break gameweek across the last five seasons would have lost 3.4 units. That is a nasty little trend for short-priced favourites to carry into the weekend.

Nottingham Forest are worth a swing at 7/2 with Sky Bet. They are due a bit of variance in their favour with the expected points table showing they should have picked up nine points more than they've got. Oliver Glasner will get them winning. And it could start here.

Nottingham Forest forward Igor Jesus has returned to training after a calf problem and could feature on Saturday. Dan Ndoye was ill in the week but should be available while Daniel Munoz is managing a minor foot injury.

Nicolas Domínguez is set for several weeks on the sidelines after a setback.

articles.title: Inter 1-4 Man City: Andree Jeglertz's side secure first win of European campaign ahead of huge WSL clash with Chelsea
articles.summary: Report as Manchester City beat Inter Milan 4-1 in the Women's Champions League; Aoba Fujino scored twice as City came from behind to secure victory; the win marks City's first European triumph of the season
articles.body:
Three draws from the first three league phase games left Andree Jeglertz's side at risk of missing out on a seeded spot in the play-off round, let alone automatic qualification for the last eight. However, an Aoba Fujino brace set them on their way to a 4-1 victory in Monza.

With a WSL clash against Chelsea on the horizon, Jeglertz opted to leave key players Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw and Lauren Hemp on the bench. That decision came under scrutiny when Inter full-back Elisa Bartoli headed the hosts into a shock lead before the half-hour mark.

City were quick to respond, however, as Laura Blindkilde Brown's pinpoint pass found Fujino's run, with the Japanese forward drawing the visitors level and opening the floodgates. The 22-year-old then completed the turnaround before half-time, and from that point onwards, there was only ever going to be one winner.

Stand-in captain Kerstin Casparij added a smart third before Grace Clinton scored a confidence-boosting fourth to round out the scoring and handed City a vital first three points of their European campaign.

The win sees City move up to seventh in the league phase table, above Real Madrid and just one point outside of the coveted top four spot.

8: SAVE! Fujino fires warning shot with early chance.

24: GOAL! City stunned as Bartoli heads Inter ahead.

33: GOAL! Fujino equalises for visitors.

38: WIDE! Fowler misses great chance to put City ahead.

44: GOAL! Fujino on the end of Fowler rebound to complete turnaround.

56: GOAL! Smart finish from Casparij to give City breathing space.

70: GOAL! Clinton gets on the end of Hemp's cross to make it four.

Manchester City defender Kerstin Casparij speaking with Disney+:

"It feels great. Inter played well and it is a tough game away from home. Two wins on the bounce makes us feel great coming into Chelsea, which will be a tough week and game.

"We've got our work cut out for us. We know what we need to bring, especially today starting with quite a few rotational players and I think we did phenomenally.

"Let's get through to the knockout stages and we will go from there."

City send message to Chelsea ahead of all-important WSL clash

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

It was clear that Andree Jeglertz had Saturday's clash with Chelsea in mind when opting to rest several key players in Monza. However, delivering such a dominant performance without the likes of Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw sends a statement in itself.

Couple that with the fact Sonia Bompastor's side limped to a drab stalemate against BK Hacken earlier in the evening, momentum is well and truly with the reigning WSL champions heading into that all-important meeting at Stamford Bridge.

Anything other than a defeat in that game would mean Jeglertz's side retain top spot, but on the basis of what they showed both against Inter and throughout the course of the season, they won't be settling for that.

Fujino's brace served as a timely reminder that City's attacking threat extends well beyond the usual headline names, giving Chelsea even more to consider ahead of Saturday's clash.

However, City were not entirely convincing defensively, with several spells of sloppy play offering Inter opportunities to threaten. The hosts' poor finishing spared the visitors from conceding further goals, with their inability to capitalise on those chances arguably the only positive Chelsea can take from an otherwise disappointing evening.

articles.title: OFFSIDE | Why Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal legacy is much more than goals and numbers
articles.summary: Albert Einstein showed beyond doubt that time wasn’t absolute, as Isaac Newton believed – trust a former German citizen to ruin an Englishman’s conception
articles.body: Albert Einstein showed beyond doubt that time wasn’t absolute, as Isaac Newton believed – trust a former German citizen to ruin an Englishman’s conception of the universe – but for now, without access to vehicles that move at the speed of light, the absolute and linear concept of time is the only human experience that exists without taking psychedelic substances. And sadly, that means slowly, the greats who have defined the last two decades of sports are slowly being put out to pasture in retirement. In tennis, Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal – two gentlemen who redefined both the game and the art of being gentlemen – have hung up their rackets. We will never see their contrasting games – Renaissance painter with a racket vs a Davidian sculpture made with a chisel – ever come up against one another. The same goes for football, where Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have now both hung up their international footballing boots.Both careers played out in the Age of Social Media, and much has been written – even in Offside – about Ronaldo’s insouciant petulance in the last days of his career, but remembrances should be about good things, not bad ones.In earlier editions of Offside, we have argued that Portugal needed to put its GOAT out to pasture, written about Spain handing Ronaldo a reality check, and lamented how watching Ronaldo had become painful, even for a Ronaldo fan. This time, we will remember the happiness he gave us.For once, let’s stop being captivated by the carousel of constant negativity and remember what the boy from Madeira – that’s closer to Morocco than Lisbon – meant to Portugal as a player.Now, much has been written about his numbers. Ronaldo has scored in six World Cups and five Euros, and has scored in 23 consecutive years. Of Portugal’s total goals at major tournaments, he has scored 19.2 per cent. There’s a very clear Portugal before Ronaldo, which, despite the likes of Luis Figo and Co, barely made a dent in tournaments, and a Portugal after Ronaldo, which looked like a team of substance.It’s also unlikely – unless Romelu Lukaku or Harry Kane go on Ronaldo-like scoring sprees – that anyone will beat his record of 146 international goals. But football isn’t about numbers: little kids don’t dream of xGs but of how the beautiful game makes us feel.There are moments in the Ronaldo highlight reel where fans and the wider footballing public were drawn in by the remarkable drama that followed.Like Euro 2004 – the same year his future Manchester United wingman and footballing soulmate Wayne Rooney burst onto the stage – when Ronaldo wept after losing to Greece in the final. Or the World Cup two years later, when Ronaldo winked at his bench after ensuring Rooney got sent off for playing with a different set of balls – before dispatching the penalty that knocked England out of the World Cup. He would come back as Public Enemy Number 1 in the UK, something that the wily Sir Alex Ferguson used to his advantage to forge the world-beating generation of Ronaldo and Co, including the 2008 Ballon d’Or that fans voted the greatest Ballon d’Or of all time.Or when he sat heartbroken – a moth fluttering over his nose after he got injured – as Portugal somehow pulled through to beat France in the Euro 2016 final that became as famous for Ronaldo’s managerial theatrics as it did for Portugal’s first major trophy. And then, while going to collect the trophy, he spotted Sir Alex, who hugged him like a Biblical prodigal son returning home.Or the 2014 World Cup qualifier showdown between Ronaldo and Zlatan – when Portugal met Sweden – which saw Ronaldo drag Portugal into the World Cup by sheer willpower.Then there was 2018, when one hat-trick appeared to cause a glitch in David de Gea’s goalkeeping algorithm – before that he was impossible to beat, and afterwards he kept getting beaten like Onana – in which Portugal drew 3-3 with Spain.The man named after Ronald Reagan would turn up for his nation whenever required, scoring when everything looked lost, and would add two UEFA Nations League titles. Yes, his tantrums would be panned on social media; at times, his overall global fame perhaps became detrimental and overshadowed the Portuguese national team’s fortunes.But there’s no doubt that because of Cristiano Ronaldo, Portugal became the team to watch and support for millions of fans across the globe.When Ronaldo first played for Portugal in August 2003, he came on as a substitute for Luís Figo, the man who was then the country's greatest footballing superstar. Ronaldo would eventually inherit Figo's No. 7 shirt, a number already associated with Portuguese footballing greatness.While Figo crossed the Barcelona-Madrid divide and got a pig’s head thrown at him for his lack of loyalty, Ronaldo, after winning everything with Manchester United, became the world’s most expensive footballer when he joined Real Madrid, which seems like a bargain at GBP 80 million, making him slightly cheaper than what Manchester United paid for Antony. During his time in Madrid, he won four Champions Leagues and well surpassed Figo’s record there. His shirt became one of the most recognised in the world.In his retirement announcement, Ronaldo spoke about handing back the No. 7 shirt, which he had worn for 23 years. It was a rather poignant admission from a man who had spent much of his career appearing almost invincible. The shirt that once belonged to Figo, and then became synonymous with Ronaldo, will now belong to someone else.When Ronaldo inherited Figo’s shirt, an entire generation of football fans was still growing up. Those same fans are now adults, many with children of their own, who have spent their lives watching Ronaldo defy age, expectations and occasionally common sense. For them, his retirement also marks the end of a part of their own lives.There will be other great Portuguese footballers, other No. 7s and perhaps even someone who breaks Ronaldo's extraordinary records. But the next player to wear that shirt will inherit an enormous burden of expectations. The No. 7 shirt has become something of a poisoned chalice at Manchester United since Ronaldo left for Madrid, and it proved to be a burden even for Ronaldo himself when he returned. Hopefully, it won’t become an albatross for the next Portuguese player who puts it on.Ronaldo’s footballing legacy will outlast the goals he has scored, the appearances he has made and the trophies he has won with club and country. Go to any corner of the world and you’ll find some random kid leaping into the air and copying his celebration. And that is something no statistic can measure. Einstein showed us that time isn’t absolute. We still don’t have a time machine or a way to travel at anything close to the speed of light. But watch those old Ronaldo highlights from our youth, and for a few fleeting moments, the years seem to disappear. We are young again, watching the man who gave us so much happiness. And we all go SIUUU.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany returns to Bayern training ground for first time since collapse
articles.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany returned to the club's training ground on Tuesday for the first time since collapsing during a practice session last
articles.body: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany returned to the club's training ground on Tuesday for the first time since collapsing during a practice session last month, taking another step towards his return to the touchline.The 40-year-old visited Bayern's Säbener Street complex for medical appointments, according to Kicker magazine. He is expected to resume his duties after the international break, with the club hoping to have him back for their Bundesliga match against Cologne on November 20.Bayern had no team training on Tuesday as most of the players were away on international duty. Club veteran Uli Hoeneß had said on Sunday that Kompany would be back in time for the Cologne game.What happened to Kompany?Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching a training session and was taken to hospital. He was diagnosed with meningeal irritation, an inflammation of the tissue surrounding the brain or spinal cord. The Belgian had also been recovering from a viral infection and a hip injury.His return to the training ground is an encouraging development as he continues his recovery, although he is yet to resume full coaching duties.Bayern maintain winning run in his absenceAssistant coach Aaron Danks stepped in to manage the team while Kompany was away. Bayern have largely done well under his charge, recording victories against Freiburg, Magdeburg, Atletico Madrid and Mainz.Their only setback during this period was a 2-2 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga's much-anticipated Der Klassiker on October 31.Bayern will now hope to have Kompany back in the dugout for the Cologne fixture as they look to continue their strong run under the Belgian coach.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Lazy' Man City charges claim rebuffed as Premier League punishment wait continues amid appeal
articles.summary: A sport integrity expert has weighed in on the delay in any potential punishment(s) heading Manchester City's way for alleged breaches of the Premier League'...
articles.body:
A sport integrity expert has emphasized that delays in publishing Manchester City's punishment for violating the Premier League's financial regulations are not because decision-makers are 'lazy'. Back in September, it was confirmed that City had been found guilty of nearly all of the Premier League charges brought against them.

The independent panel determined City had intended to breach financial rules by inflating revenues or reducing costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion at the current exchange rate), through a series of 'sham' arrangements. City have appealed the decision and have maintained their innocence.

As the appeal process unfolds, City fans have anxiously been awaiting their club's punishment. Given the volume of charges and the unprecedented nature of the case, several 'likely' sanctions have been discussed including; substantial points deductions, transfer bans, expulsion from the Premier League, and fines.

But speaking to the Press Association, co-founder and global chief executive of Sport Integrity Global Alliance (SIGA), Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros stressed the priority must be for justice to be served, rather than for a swift outcome to be achieved, as per the Manchester Evening News .

"I understand the fans' frustration, and I understand also the fans' anguish, especially those who follow and support Manchester City," he said.

"This is not a pleasant situation for anybody, but the law is the law, and it must be served on its own time, without constraints. Being a lawyer, I know that justice sometimes is served slowly. That is not because those who are in charge of the procedures are lazy, or they neglect their duties. It's because there cannot be room for doubt. There cannot be room for failure.

"There cannot be any breach of the constitutional rights that those who are being scrutinised or judged enjoy. But I think it's fair to say that the process is coming to an end."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

The verdict determined that City operated a 'disguised funding scheme' whereby Abu Dhabi-based companies contributed only a portion of the figures recorded in the club's accounts, with the remaining balance covered by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), the vehicle through which Sheikh Mansour holds ownership of the club. This arrangement was found to have artificially inflated revenues by more than £830 million ($1.1 billion) across the nine-season stretch between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

City were additionally found to have overstated image rights income by almost £74 million ($98.8 million), and understated staff contract liabilities by almost £17 million ($22.7 million). In response, the Blues maintained the ruling contained 'clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe'.

Club CEO Ferran Soriano addressed staff via video, asserting that the panel had sided with the Premier League's 'conspiracy theory'.

articles.title: Jacobo Ramón: "Sabía que había llegado mi momento de salir del Real Madrid"
articles.standfirst: Jacobo Ramón cuenta en La Tribu de Radio MARCA cómo le convenció Cesc Fàbregas para fichar por el Como y por qué el vestuario está “a muerte con la idea del míster”
articles.summary: Jacobo Ramón cuenta en La Tribu de Radio MARCA cómo le convenció Cesc Fàbregas para fichar por el Como y por qué el vestuario está “a muerte con la idea del míster”
articles.body: Jacobo Ramón tenía 8 años cuando llegó al Real Madrid y llevaba doce en el club cuando decidió salir para demostrar qué clase de central podía ser lejos de Valdebebas. Encontró su sitio en el Como de Cesc Fàbregas y ahora afronta su primera convocatoria con la selección española sabiendo que el Real Madrid le tiene en el radar para el futuro. El central del Como echa la vista atrás tras su salida del Real Madrid en una entrevista en Radio MARCA que se emitirá este miércoles antes de La Tribu: "Sabía que había llegado mi momento. Es muy difícil estar en el primer equipo, la competencia es máxima y creo que tenía que demostrar fuera el jugador que era. Di el paso correcto en el momento justo y, de momento, me está saliendo bien". Jacobo Ramón reconoce que el Como le sedujo y más con Cesc al mando: "El proyecto era muy ambicioso. El año pasado ya hicimos una temporada muy buena y conseguimos clasificarnos para la Champions. Y, por supuesto, Cesc: me llamó, me contó su idea de juego y creo que encajaba perfectamente con el futbolista que soy. Esto tiene un autor, que es Cesc. Está trabajando muy bien con nosotros". El central madrileño de 21 años afirma sobre su estreno en la concentración que "soy algo tímido y me lo están poniendo muy fácil. Huijsen ha estado bastante pendiente de mí y Cubarsí se ha sentado conmigo en la mesa. En general, todos me han ayudado mucho". Y Jacobo no quiere mirar al futuro, donde le puede esperar su regreso al Real Madrid, sino pensar en el presente que tiene por delante en el Como y la selección: "Ahora mismo estoy centrado en el Como. Tenemos una temporada muy bonita por delante. Estamos en noviembre, prácticamente acabamos de empezar, y ya tenemos bastante con lo que tenemos en Italia. De verdad que no pienso en eso". El nuevo central de La Roja no oculta que las críticas en las redes sociales tras su debut de blanco en Leganés las pudo superar: "La primera vez siempre te afecta más. El Madrid es el equipo más expuesto del mundo y, si no lo haces bien y los resultados no acompañan, sabes que te van a criticar. Lo importante es superarlo y que no te afecte de cara al futuro. Cada uno puede tener su opinión, pero un futbolista no se demuestra en 45 minutos".

articles.title: La Copa le sirve al Valencia para jugar, ganar, sanar... y callar
articles.standfirst: Los de Aguirre aprovechan la Copa para estrenarse en Mestalla con un festival de goles (Raba, Duro, Elliot, Rioja y Aimar 2) y debuts ante el Tavernes
articles.summary: Los de Aguirre aprovechan la Copa para estrenarse en Mestalla con un festival de goles (Raba, Duro, Elliot, Rioja y Aimar 2) y debuts ante el Tavernes
articles.body: Treinta y cuatro segundos. Ni uno más ni uno menos. Ese fue el tiempo que duró el empate en Mestalla entre el Tavernes y el Valencia. Este modelo de Copa, al menos en los primeros cruces, tiene poca chicha deportiva. Más aún cuando el partido, para hacer taquilla, se juega en casa del equipo grande perdiendo así parte de la magia. Con cinco categorías de diferencia pensar que el Tavernes podía hacerle un rasguño al Valencia era estúpido, más aún con la sensación de urgencia con la que los de Aguirre saltaban al campo de Mestalla. Sacar conclusiones reales de este partido sería hacerse trampas al solitario. Como dijo Aguirre, jugar y callar. En este caso añadiendo ganar y golear, que tampoco está de más. Así las cosas, en el primer balón del partido Sato filtró un paso en profundidad para que Aimar diera el pase de la muerte a un Raba que no falló. Pocos minutos después marcó Hugo Duro al primer toque tras una gran asistencia de Raba. Cero a dos y abrazos para el delantero que necesita algo de cariño tras un inicio de temporada que le ha dejado triturado y hundido en el banquillo. Era un día para marcar y liberarse y Rioja hizo el tercero cuando aún no se habían jugado veinte minutos. Poco después llegó el gol de Elliott de falta, buen golpeo del británico. Tras el cuarto del inglés, el partido cayó en intensidad para evitar hacer demasiado daño a un equipo que metió miles de aficionados en las gradas de Mestalla. La segunda mitad arrancó con algo más de pausa. Buenas paradas de Mainar y un disparo de Eric a la salida de un córner que se estrelló en el palo. La ocasión del Tavernes se celebró en la grada a lo grande. La llegada tuvo mérito, pero pronto se vio ensombrecida por un nuevo gol del Valencia, esta vez de Aimar Blázquez tras un gran pase de Rioja. Lo había buscado el canterano. El delantero repitió diana, otra vez tras asistencia de Rioja, para firmar un doblete que muestra que tiene el gol que el equipo busca. El partido acabó con besos y abrazos y ambiente excepcional en la grada. Los más de 20.000 hinchas del Tavernes que se desplazaron a Mestalla se lo pasaron en grande y los valencianistas que se acercaron hasta completar los 32.000 espectadores vieron la primera victoria en casa de los suyos esta temporada, contra un equipo de preferente sí, pero victoria al fin y al cabo.

articles.title: Zubimendi: "No me he puesto en contacto con nadie ni estoy cerca de nadie"
articles.standfirst: El mediocentro de la selección y del Arsenal se sienta con MARCA y niega que sus planes pasen por dejar Londres
articles.summary: El mediocentro de la selección y del Arsenal se sienta con MARCA y niega que sus planes pasen por dejar Londres
articles.body: Martín Zubimendi (San Sebastián, 2-2-1999) tiene una sonrisa constante en la cara. En las buenas y en las malas. De él dicen que es discreto, casi hasta la exageración. Su vida ha dado un cambio radical en un año. De jugarlo todo con el Arsenal a sumar apenas 100 minutos en lo que va de Premier. Eso ha hecho que su nombre se haya convertido en un clásico en las informaciones de mercado. Primero el Madrid, ahora el Atlético. La sonrisa no se borra de la cara, pero no oculta que está molesto. "No hay nada de nada, ni estoy cerca de nada", asegura a MARCA.. PREGUNTA. En nuestro Forjados decía su amiga Naiaa que es una persona a la que le gusta pasar desapercibida. ¿Es así? R. Sí. Cuando estoy con mi entorno y con la gente cercana soy un poco diferente, pero sí que tiendo a ser discreto, a no llamar la atención y a no estar siempre en primera línea. P. También hablaban de su sentido del humor inteligente. R. Lo puedo llegar a entender. A veces me gusta darle una vuelta más a las bromas y, de vez en cuando, sale algo gracioso. ¿Mala leche? Eso no. P. ¿Cómo está ahora mismo, jugando mucho menos de lo esperado? R. Bien, tranquilo y contento con cómo estoy llevando esta situación. Es algo que no había vivido hasta ahora y creo que de estas situaciones también se aprende. Además, en momentos así es cuando más necesitas a la gente que tienes alrededor y ahí están. P. ¿Qué ha descubierto de si mismo en este tiempo? R. Que soy paciente. Cuando vienes de jugar muchos minutos y te cambia el rol a no jugar tanto, estoy siendo capaz de ver el lado positivo. Pienso que todo pasa, que igual que el año pasado me ocurrió lo contrario y lo jugué prácticamente todo, esto puede cambiar muy rápido. P. El año pasado jugaba siempre y de repente desaparecen los minutos. ¿Desgaste físico? R. No me gusta achacarlo todo al físico, pero sí que ese año lo noté bastante. Fue un año nuevo para mí, con muchos estímulos nuevos. Jugué una barbaridad de minutos y la verdad es que estaba cansado. Luego también hubo otras cosas, pero una de ellas pudo ser perfectamente el aspecto físico. P. ¿Ha pensado en recurrir a ayuda psicológica? R. Me lo he planteado y no lo descarto, pero de momento no he tocado esa puerta. P. ¿Habla de estas situaciones con el entrenador? ¿Con Arteta o con Luis de la Fuente? R. Sí. Con Mikel hablé a principios de temporada. Como hace con todos los jugadores, me explicó un poco el plan. Me advirtió de que había fichajes nuevos y de que habría minutos para todos. Y ahí estamos, peleando. P. Mikel Merino sostiene que la competencia en el Arsenal es salvaje. R. Lo entiendo porque para mí estamos entre los cinco mejores equipos de Europa. Hay grandísimos jugadores. En mi posición han llegado fichajes y ya había futbolistas muy buenos. Yo también formo parte de esa competencia que hace tan difícil jugar. P. Como no juega todo lo que la gente esperaba, aparecen muchos rumores. ¿Está tranquilo? R. Sí. No he gastado energía en cosas de fuera. Bastante tengo con intentar ganarme un puesto, tener minutos y luchar por ganar esta Premier, que pinta tan bien. No he gastado energía en ello ni me he puesto en contacto con nadie. P. Se ha publicado que está muy cerca del Atlético de Madrid. R. La verdad es que a mí también me sorprende a veces la prensa. Entiendo que llega el mercado de invierno y pueden aparecer rumores, pero creo que hay que tener un poco más de cuidado con lo que se publica. Al final cada uno tiene un equipo en el que juega y hay que tener respeto. Yo también he leído que podía estar cerca, pero ni mucho menos. P. ¿Te molestan esas informaciones? R. Sí, la verdad es que sí. Muchas veces sale una noticia y parece que, si no se cumple, se olvida rápido y no pasa nada. Voy conociendo cómo funciona este mundo y lo voy naturalizando, pero a veces me podría ahorrar muchos mensajes que me llegan por culpa de este tipo de noticias. P. ¿Qué ocurre cuando sale una información así? R. Que incluso yo mismo tengo que entrar en Twitter para ver exactamente qué ha salido y poder responder a la gente que me pregunta. P. Ahora que el Madrid vuela ya no se habla de que necesita a Zubimendi... R. Lo entiendo. Creo que forma parte del fútbol, de los momentos y de las noticias. A la gente también le gusta todo esto. P. ¿Está feliz en Londres? R. Sí, estoy contento. P. Volviendo a la selección. En el Mundial terminó participando en la final después de no haber jugado antes. Cuando el seleccionador dice que todos tienen que estar preparados, ¿hay que creérselo de verdad? R. Sí. En la Eurocopa, aunque había jugado poco, al menos había tenido minutos en la fase de grupos. En este Mundial no había jugado ninguno, pero iba con la esperanza de que me pudiera tocar. No sé si era de iluso, pero yo pensaba que podía jugar algunos minutos. Y al final tocó. P. El gol de Oyarzabbal fue con Zubimendi en el campo; el de Ferran, también. R. Son momentos que me llevaré para siempre. Estar dentro del campo en acciones tan importantes y poder celebrarlo desde dentro fue algo muy bonito. También me permitió quitarme un poco esa espinita. P. Luis de la Fuente suele decir que no valoramos suficientemente lo que tenemos en España. R. Creo que ahora estamos en un muy buen momento y que al jugador español se le valora mucho por todo lo conseguido. Es verdad que cuando no se ganan títulos tan importantes es más difícil, pero ahora mismo siento que se nos respeta mucho. P. ¿Qué valor le da al Balón de Oro? R. Es un premio individual y quien diga que no, alguna vez ha soñado con ganarlo. Aunque sea subjetivo porque lo votan muchas personas diferentes relacionadas con el fútbol, es algo bonito y seguramente lo máximo a lo que puede aspirar un jugador a nivel individual. P. ¿Compartir selección con Rodri es una bendición o un problema? R. Una bendición. En parte gracias a él también tengo los títulos que tengo. Ha sido un jugador clave en todos los torneos que hemos disputado. Si me va dejando algunos minutos intentaré aprovecharlos, pero entiendo perfectamente que es un jugador de talla mundial y el mejor en su puesto. P. Llega ahora el partido ante la República Checa. La gente ve la racha, los partidos sin perder, las cifras... ¿Cómo lo vive el equipo? R. Como un partido más, aunque es verdad que es un dato que siempre aparece en las previas. Si no hubiera motivación suficiente, ya sería un aliciente más para seguir ampliando la racha. Estamos en un momento en el que la podemos llevar mucho más lejos. P. ¿Se habla de ello en el vestuario? R. No demasiado. Es más el míster quien intenta ponernos en contexto sobre dónde estamos y a qué podemos aspirar. Entre nosotros, en las comidas y demás, no solemos hablar de esos datos. P. Para terminar, ¿seguirá en el Arsenal hasta final de temporada? R. Sí, espero que sí. Estoy contento allí. P. ¿Hasta cuándo tiene contrato? R. Hasta 2030.

articles.title: EFL Trophy: Leicester City and Brentford U21 into knockout stages
articles.summary: Brentford U21 and League One side Leicester City move into the knockout stages of the Jersey Mike's Trophy with vital victories.
articles.body:
Brentford U21 and League One side Leicester City both moved into the knockout stages of the Jersey Mike's Trophy with vital victories.

The Bees had to beat the Football League's basement side Crawley Town in their final fixture in Southern Group H to progress and did so courtesy of a Domeiro Bobb-Semple double in a 2-1 success at Broadfield Stadium, where Connor Wickham scored on his Crawley debut.

In Southern Group B, the Foxes trailed at the King Power Stadium against League Two Walsall, who would have gone through in place of their hosts with a win. But strikes from Will Smallbone and John Lundstram put them ahead by the break and they held on.

Stevenage topped the group by beating Fulham U21 on penalties.

Chelsea U21 were not in action but went through at the expense of Reading , who needed a big win away against Bristol Rovers to see them overtake the west London side in Southern Group C, but the Royals were beaten on penalties.

Nottingham Forest U21 and Notts County both eased through into the last 16 with wins in Northern Group F.

Forest enjoyed a 3-0 success against League Two promotion-chasers Grimsby Town at Blundell Park, where all the goals came before the break.

The Magpies moved into the knockout stages as group winners by beating League One Burton Albion by the same scoreline for a third win in three EFL Trophy games.

In Southern Group F, Leyton Orient needed a big victory over Barnet to claim an unlikely second-placed finish on goal difference, but they were well beaten at The Hive, with Jack Maskell's first-half strike setting the hosts on the way to a 4-2 win.

Oxford United coasted to a 4-0 win over Cheltenham Town to go second in Southern Group A - and will stay there as long as they avoid a heavy defeat against Tottenham Hotspur U21 in their final fixture.

In Southern Group G, Gillingham made sure of their place in the last 32 by seeing off Northampton Town 2-1. The Gills only needed a point to be certain of finishing in second place above Brighton & Hove Albion U21, but Lamin Sillah scored one goal and made another to inspire his side to victory over their League Two rivals.

Seb Campbell crashed home a 99th-minute winner as Plymouth Argyle beat Swindon Town at Home Park to finish top of the pile in Southern Group E, while Colchester United beat Ipswich Town U21 on penalties after a 0-0 draw in Southern Group D, in a match where both sides knew their campaign had ended after their second fixture.

Elsewhere, a close-range shot by Tom Graves put Crewe Alexandra on track for the win they needed to progress from Northern Group B, but Wigan Athletic scored twice in the second half to dash their hopes, while veteran forward Nick Powell was among the scorers as Bradford City thumped York City 4-0 to top Northern Group C.

In a thriller in Northern Group D, already eliminated Mansfield Town looked set for their first points of the competition as they led already qualified Chesterfield 3-1 with 28 minutes remaining. But Dylan Duffy scored two of four goals in the closing stages to earn the Spireites a remarkable 5-3 victory.

Stockport County beat Tranmere Rovers on penalties in Northern Group E, but both sides were already sure of qualification, while Huddersfield Town thumped Liverpool U21 4-0 to finish top of Northern Group H.

articles.standfirst: El centrocampista habla de su rol actual en el Barça de Flick
articles.summary: El centrocampista habla de su rol actual en el Barça de Flick
articles.body: Marc Bernal habló de su rol actual en el Barça de Hansi Flick, de las consecuencias que ha tenido para él el fichaje de Rodri el pasado verano o de su relación con Lamine Yamal. En una entrevista en "El Partidazo" de la cadena COPE, el centrocampista azulgrana reconoció que le sorprendió mucho ver a Frenkie de Jong de lateral el pasado encuentro en el Metropolitano. "Yo le pregunté a Frenkie y me dijo que salía de lateral derecho. Me quedé sorprendido pero lo cierto es que jugó muy bien". "Yo lo miré de dos formas: primero tengo al mejor pivote del mundo y puedo aprender mucho de él. La segunda es que me quitaba muchos minutos. El club me transmitió tranquilidad y eso significó mucho porque tampoco tiene porqué hacerlo. Lo fichan y ya está. Es verdad que te quita minutos. Lo llevo bien, intento fijarme en lo que hace él y cómo es. Es un líder dentro del grupo. Es muy fácil llevarse con él. Yo tengo 19 años y él tiene 30. Me quedan muchos años de carrera. Me jode porque no voy a tener minutos pero tampoco es lo que quiero ya, no me como la cabeza". "Para mí el mejor equipo es el Barça. Es verdad que perdimos con el Madrid, pero un partido no marca eso. Para mí el PSG no es mejor tampoco. Si jugamos contra el PSG en casa, ¿tú crees que nos ganan? Yo confío en que les podemos ganar más adelante. Siendo honesto, si estamos bien y sin lesionados, podemos ganarles". "Tenemos muy buena relación. Es muy cercano. Me mandó mensajes cuando me lesioné o cuando fui con la absoluta. Yo no hablo nada de inglés y él habla poco. Si tenemos que hablar de algo, suele haber un traductor". "Estuve desde prebenjamín con él. Siempre hemos sido amigos, nos llevamos muy bien. Tantos años jugando juntos haces amistad".

articles.title: Real Madrid's Vinicius Jr sends surprise message to Sudanese boy who lost his legs in war
articles.summary: Double amputee Zaher told the BBC last year about his favourite footballer and a dream of being able to walk again.
articles.body:
In a dark room in Cairo, a 13-year-old boy looks up at a television screen, barely blinking.

The screen flickers and Real Madrid's superstar winger Vinícius Júnior appears addressing the young boy directly, in Arabic: "Zaher, mahaba" - Hello Zaher.

Zaher barely moves, his eyes wide, locked on his favourite footballer.

We first met Zaher a year ago in the ruins of Sudan's capital, Khartoum. He was a small quiet child, scarred by war - one of millions of children whose lives have been upended since the country's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) started fighting in 2023.

More than 17 million children are now in need of humanitarian assistance in Sudan, according to the UN children's charity, Unicef. It says it has been able to verify that at least 4,300 have been killed or maimed, although it believes the true figure is far higher.

Zaher had lost both his legs in a drone strike. With little access to specialist treatment, he dreamed of the day he might walk and play football again.

More than a year later, as we walk into an apartment in the Egyptian capital, Zaher greets us with an enormous hug. His mother, Habibah, embraces us too.

The boy we remember as shy and withdrawn is almost unrecognisable. He is confident, cheeky and full of smiles. And he is standing tall on two new prosthetic legs.

For almost a year, Cairo has been his home. Here, he has undergone surgery and months of rehabilitation, and is now able to walk and kick a ball again.

When we met in 2025, he had told us his favourite footballer was Vinícius Júnior. We were able to pass this on to the Real Madrid star, who said he wanted to send a personal video message of support. Reunited in Cairo, we gather round to watch it together.

"I was made aware of your story. I know how difficult the last few months must have been for you," the Brazilian footballer begins.

Vinícius has become a leading voice challenging racism in football and supporting black people, and a smile spreads across Zaher's face as the player tells him: "You are a hard-working black man. I really hope you will make good use of your new prosthetic legs, that you return to playing football and that you find happiness. You deserve it."

Then comes an invitation: "I would like to invite you to attend a Madrid match. We can spend the day together."

Overwhelmed, Zaher gets up and leaves the room. A few moments later, he returns wearing his new Vinícius Jr football shirt. He hopes that one day he will be able to get a visa and accept the offer.

"Tell Vinícius, I love him," he says. "His message has really uplifted me." His mother Habibah says she feels "like the whole world is cheering Zaher on, wanting him to succeed".

Zaher lost his legs in 2024, when he and his mother had been trapped in Khartoum. Much of the city had become a battleground as it was torn apart by fighting between Sudan's army and the RSF.

Food and basic supplies were running short and the family did not have enough money to flee. To survive, they sold lentils on the streets.

Then one morning, as Zaher and his mother worked side by side, a drone struck.

"I looked at him and he was bleeding. There was blood everywhere," Habibah explained last year.

She was devastated. "He would wake up and ask: 'Why did you let them cut off my legs?' I couldn't answer."

Back then, Zaher was wheeling himself through the rubble of his neighbourhood in a wheelchair, past burnt-out cars, abandoned tanks and shattered homes.

Before the war, Zaher had loved football. After the drone strike, he could only play on his knees, a painful process that put him at risk of serious infection.

"I wish I could have prosthetic legs so I can play football with my friends like I used to," he said at the time .

There seemed little prospect of that happening, but his story resonated far beyond Sudan, prompting an outpouring of support from people around the world.

Among them was Dena Latif, a UK-based lawyer of Sudanese origin. After seeing the BBC report, she helped spearhead an online campaign raising £45,000 ($60,000) for his medical care.

Unable to get the treatment he needed in Sudan, Zaher had to leave the country, which was far from straightforward. He and his mother had no passports and their birth certificates had been destroyed during the war.

After months of planning, he and his mother were able to fly to Cairo where an apartment had been prepared for them, with food in the fridge and medical appointments arranged.

For the first time in years, their immediate concern was no longer simply how to survive.

'I can't afford to save both twins': Sudan's war left one mother with an impossible choice

A simple guide to what is happening in Sudan

Zaher underwent further surgery, followed by months of physiotherapy and training to learn to use his prosthetic legs. He also received psychological support to help him process the trauma he had been through.

"He was shy, a little bit depressed, sad," says Dr Bintelmuna Eltayeb , one of the doctors involved in his care. "To get a smile out of him was almost impossible, but now you can see he's laughing. He has great confidence in himself."

His transformation has been as much psychological as physical, say those close to him, and Dena says Zaher now approaches life with a determination that has surprised them.

As we spend time with Zaher, he laughs and jokes, making up for some of the childhood that war has taken from him.

He is eager to try new things, from horse riding to cycling, and wants to become an airline pilot. He hasn't had a game of football yet but is looking forward to playing with his friends back home.

For Habibah, watching her son regain his confidence has brought enormous relief. But she worries about his future, his education and how he will be received in Sudan, a country still locked in civil war.

The state of emergency has been lifted in their home city, Khartoum, with the Sudanese army back in control there. But throughout the capital, buildings have been left destroyed - burned, blackened and looted.

Concerns over security remain and 41% of Sudan's population are experiencing high levels of food insecurity, according to a recent statement released by the US and 30 other Western states. The group also warned of "potential famine" .

"I hope that Zaher's story doesn't end with him," says Dena. She hopes his recovery will attract more attention and funds for the thousands of other Sudanese children who have suffered life-altering injuries.

Zaher and his mother are now back in Khartoum. They hope that as the city is more stable at the moment, he will be able to get his prosthetic legs checked and adjusted there as he grows.

Despite the safety they found in Cairo, they missed their home, family and friends. And while Zaher has been given a chance to reclaim his childhood, millions of other Sudanese children are still waiting for theirs.

articles.title: ‘Not worried, God is good’: Terrell Owens speaks out after being served with defamation lawsuit from teens who were with Nolan Wells
articles.summary: The NFL Hall of Famer was celebrating his new documentary when he was served with a lawsuit over social media
articles.body:
The NFL Hall of Famer was celebrating his new documentary when he was served with a lawsuit over social media posts about the death of Mississippi teen Nolan Wells.

Terrell Owens was at his alma mater celebrating his new Amazon documentary about his life and career on Friday when he was served with a defamation lawsuit tied to a tweet earlier this summer surrounding the disappearance of Mississippi teen Nolan Wells .

Owens, a member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame, demanded the arrest of three individuals who were with Wells when he disappeared in July. The star athlete was later found dead two days later. Following an investigation and multiple autopsies, a grand jury declined to indict anyone in connection with his disappearance and death.

Under Mississippi state law, the three individuals are considered minors because they are under 21.

The suit was filed Oct. 5 on behalf of the three teens by their fathers. According to attorney Edward Paltzik of Taylor Dykema PLLC, who is representing the teens, Owens had been evading being served with the lawsuit. During the event at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga, Paltzik chose what he called a time and place Owens "least expected" to be served: homecoming.

"No autograph required. Luck always runs out," Paltzik wrote in a lengthy post on X.

On Sunday, two days after being served, Owens responded to a video of the incident on X.

"Hey Edward," he began. "Not worried. God is good."

In September, Owens posted on his X account his thoughts about an interview from "The Trent Out Loud Show" that was shared on Instagram. In the clip, the host said Mississippi Attorney General Angel Myers McIlrath knew that the teens "deleted things off of Nolan's phone."

"ARREST THEM IMMEDIATELY!!" Owens wrote. "LIKE YESTERDAY!!"

In a follow-up post on X, Owens gladly welcomed the suit. "I CAN NOT WAIT UNTIL JUSTICE IS SERVED. #JUSTICEFORNOLANWELLS," he wrote. "Hey Ed, you can't save those kids and me saying what I said is freedom of speech."

Owens has paid close attention to Wells' case, previously offering $25,000 for information "leading to the arrest and conviction of those responsible."

The teens have stated they've received death threats in connection with Wells' disappearance and have been "refused service at public establishments" and have been inundated with harassment and "daily fear and ridicule from complete strangers."

"Contrary to Owens' defamatory X post, there was absolutely no evidence to prompt an arrest of the plaintiffs because they had done nothing wrong, and there was no probable cause to arrest plaintiffs because they had not committed a crime," the suit reads.

The plaintiffs are seeking damages in this case and assert two counts: defamation per se and false light invasion of privacy.

articles.title: LSU Soccer Falls to Alabama in the Quarterfinals of the SEC Tournament
articles.summary: No. 11-seeded LSU fell to No. 3-seeded Alabama, 2-1, in the quarterfinals of the SEC Tournament
articles.body:
No. 11-seeded LSU fell to No. 3-seeded Alabama, 2-1, in the quarterfinals of the SEC Tournament on Tuesday afternoon at the Ashton Brosnaham Soccer Complex, per an official press release.

Despite a strong first-half performance from goalkeeper Audur Scheving, who recorded five saves in the opening 45 minutes, the Tigers and Crimson Tide entered halftime scoreless. Alabama outshot LSU 9-2 in the first half, but Scheving's efforts kept the match level heading into the break.

LSU increased its offensive pressure in the second half, recording 11 shots compared to just two in the opening period. However, Alabama struck first in the 69th minute when Melina Rebimbas found the back of the net off assists from Soph Martelli and Kennedy Garcia to give the Crimson Tide a 1-0 advantage.

The Tigers responded in the 80th minute when Ava Galligan scored her eighth goal of the season to even the match at 1-1. The equalizer came following a pair of blocked shots from Emma Alvord, giving LSU momentum with just over 10 minutes remaining.

Alabama regained the lead in the 87th minute when Ashley Roni converted a penalty kick to put the Crimson Tide ahead, 2-1. Despite LSU's late offensive efforts, Alabama held on to secure the victory and advance to the SEC Tournament semifinals.

Scheving finished the match with seven saves, while Galligan led the Tigers with three shots and one goal. LSU recorded 13 total shots, including 11 in the second half, while Alabama finished with 20 shots.

articles.body:
There is a new No. 1 in the College Football Playoff rankings.

While Miami checked in at No. 1 in the initial rankings, Saturday's loss to Notre Dame opened the door for others around the country. And Georgia went right through it with a commanding 42-7 victory over Ole Miss.

Here is a look at the full set of new rankings, which were released Tuesday:

This is the first set of rankings after a statement Saturday shook up the national picture with a number of important results.

Perhaps no result was more impactful than the Fighting Irish's victory over Miami, which now gives them a quality win to fall back on should they lose a second game. A loss to the Hurricanes after the previous loss to BYU would have put them in a difficult position without many quality wins to point to on the resume.

Instead, they now have one of the best wins of the season after CJ Carr bolstered his Heisman chances by throwing for 319 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions.

Elsewhere, the Bulldogs' blowout win over Ole Miss likely said something about both teams.

Georgia may be the best team in the country with a dominant defense and efficient offense, while the Rebels don't look like serious contenders following their third loss.

That is three more losses than Utah has following a rivalry win over BYU to preserve its undefeated record. Devon Dampier threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more while outplaying Bear Bachmeier and handing the Cougars a critical second loss.

Alabama also has two losses, although it remains highly ranked after an impressive road win over LSU. Lane Kiffin's team now has three losses and wasn't particularly competitive in the fourth quarter, which has the Tigers on the outside of the playoff picture.

They aren't the only ones with question marks in the SEC, as Kentucky's hot start to the season came crashing down with a blowout loss to Tennessee. It was both a massive statement for the Volunteers and a loss that will likely leave many wondering what the overall ceiling is for the Wildcats this season.

Tennessee is one of a number of contenders in the SEC, which is a list that still includes Texas after the Longhorns escaped Missouri with a win thanks to two touchdowns from Raleek Brown in the fourth quarter.

Next up is a showdown with LSU and yet another opportunity to bolster their overall standing for the 12-team field.

articles.summary: The latest 2026-27 College Football Playoff rankings released on Tuesday and featured several changes among the top teams.
articles.body:
The latest 2026-27 College Football Playoff rankings released on Tuesday and featured several changes among the top teams.

Miami fell from No. 1 to No. 7 following a 31-27 loss to Notre Dame on Saturday, while the Fighting Irish moved up from No. 11 to No. 5 as a result.

Georgia is the new No. 1 team in the CFP rankings, as the Bulldogs made a statement with a lopsided 42-7 win over No. 19 Ole Miss on Saturday.

With the 2026 regular season beginning to wind down, several schools will look to make a case for themselves as one of the 12 playoff teams in Week 11.

Ohio State sat at No. 20 in Tuesday's CFP rankings as the team prepares to face Northwestern. The Buckeyes have lost two straight games since starting quarterback Julian Sayin suffered an injury to his throwing arm , owning a 6-3 overall record.

While head coach Ryan Day's squad may still earn a CFP berth with three consecutive wins to close out the regular season, a loss to Northwestern could end Ohio State's playoff candidacy entirely.

LSU moved to No. 21 from No. 14 after suffering a 31-13 loss to Alabama on Saturday, but the Tigers have a chance to put themselves back in the playoff conversation if they're able to take down No. 6 Texas, No. 8 Tennessee and Arkansas to finish the season.

A defeat at the hands of the Longhorns in Week 11 would drop head coach Lane Kiffin's team to 6-4 and effectively end their CFP hopes, though.

Another school in danger of falling out of the playoff picture is No. 10 BYU, as the Cougars have lost two of their past three games following a 6-0 start to the season.

BYU has an opportunity to stay in contention for a CFP berth as well as the Big 12 title by defeating a Baylor squad that owns a 6-3 record in Week 11. The Cougars' playoff outlook will become extremely murky with another loss, however.

articles.title: CFP Chair Explains Latest Rankings, Alabama's Spot in Bracket Compared to Tennessee
articles.summary: The new College Football Playoff rankings were released Tuesday, and one of the first things that jumps out is two-loss Alabama being all the way up at No. 3 and ahead of undefeated UCLA, a number of one-loss teams and a two-loss Tennessee squad that beat the Crimson Tide in their head-to-head matchup.
articles.body:
The new College Football Playoff rankings were released Tuesday, and one of the first things that jumps out is two-loss Alabama being all the way up at No. 3 and ahead of undefeated UCLA, a number of one-loss teams and a two-loss Tennessee squad that beat the Crimson Tide in their head-to-head matchup.

CFP chair Hunter Yurachek addressed Alabama's position, especially compared to Tennessee, during an interview on ESPN (h/t Mike Rodak of 247Sports) and highlighted its strength of schedule.

"They're No. 1 in record strength, No. 1 in schedule strength," he said of the Crimson Tide. "They have four what we call quality wins because we continue to call that win against Mississippi State earlier in the year when they had Kamario Taylor on their team, they were 4-0. Alabama went there and won that game. Alabama we believe deserves to be the No. 3 team in the country."

He continued and said, "Alabama was in that first pool. Tennessee was not in that first pool. Tennessee has got a couple of quality wins—the win they just had at Kentucky and obviously the win they have against Alabama. They have three wins against teams their schedule strength is 110 and above.

"When you look at their schedule compared to Alabama's schedule, the committee feels like—and so do the metrics—that Alabama has got a stronger schedule. That's why Alabama was in that first pool of teams and Tennessee was not."

Alabama's victories over Kentucky and South Carolina from September have aged well, as both teams are ranked in the top 17. What's more, it handled LSU with relative ease on the road on Saturday, and the Tigers are still in the rankings at No. 21.

As for the Volunteers, they have notable wins over Alabama and Kentucky.

While the Crimson Tide are ahead of Tennessee for now, that could very well change by the end of the season if both teams continue to win. After all, Notre Dame was ahead of Miami for the majority of the CFP rankings last season despite the Hurricanes' head-to-head win just for Miami to jump the Fighting Irish in the final ones.

Tennessee's strength of schedule is also more difficult moving forward, as it plays Texas A&M on the road and then LSU before finishing with Vanderbilt. Alabama, on the other hand, faces Vanderbilt, Chattanooga and Auburn.

As long as the Volunteers keep winning, they will likely eventually pass the Crimson Tide when they are in the same pool of teams and the head-to-head becomes more important.

For now, though, there are likely some Tennessee fans who are not thrilled their team is behind Alabama despite a 26-10 head-to-head win.

articles.title: Winners and Losers of the Week 11 College Football Playoff Rankings
articles.summary: The second edition of the 2026 College Football Playoff rankings has provided a notable facelift in the Top Five.
articles.body:
The second edition of the 2026 College Football Playoff rankings has provided a notable facelift in the Top Five.

Georgia has risen to No. 1 after dismantling Ole Miss on the road, aided by Miami's loss at Notre Dame—which also emerged as one of the biggest winners in the latest Top 25 from the CFP selection committee.

The same, however, cannot be said for the ACC at large.

Nevertheless, our standard disclaimer applies: This order is destined to change. We still have three weeks remaining in the regular season, and some disagreements will naturally work themselves out in Week 11 and beyond.

Each release is a snapshot of the season, though, and we've parsed the rankings for a handful of notable takeaways.

On one hand, you can be critical about the placement of Big 12 teams.

No. 12 Texas Tech, at 8-1, is right behind two-loss Kentucky. No. 23 Arizona, at 7-2, trails a smattering of three-loss programs, and Oklahoma State—which owns a head-to-head victory over 16th-ranked Oregon—is the final team in the Top 25.

Unlike the ACC, however—and more on that league shortly—the Big 12 can take solace in the simple fact of having five schools in the ranking.

In short: It means the committee actually has some respect for the conference.

Utah is second nationally, while BYU is 10th and Houston is 14th. Neither of the latter have a ranked opponent left on their respective slates, either.

At this moment, the Big 12 has a very realistic path to a pair of CFP invitations.

As a reminder, the highest-ranked Group of Six program will automatically earn a spot in the 2026 College Football Playoff. That doesn't necessarily need to be a G6 conference champion, though it likely will be.

Boise State, as it stands, is the team to beat.

The lone G6 school included in last week's ranking at No. 25, Boise State merely rose to 24th on Tuesday. No other G6 team appeared in the ranking.

We know the CFP is heavily slanted toward power-conference schools. That has been abundantly clear for years.

But what else does New Mexico need to accomplish? The squad is 8-1 with only an eight-point loss on the road to Oklahoma—which, sure, isn't an awesome team in 2026 yet was good enough to beat sixth-ranked Texas, plus Florida last week.

Instead, the Lobos are unranked as seven 6-3 teams made the Top 25.

Checking in 13th—the very middle of the Top 25—in the initial poll, Tennessee rightfully should have been perplexed at its position last week.

Yes, the Vols had fallen at South Carolina days before. Sure, there was a setback to Texas on their résumé. The CFP committee probably could have justified a dozen different orders in the 5-15 range, as well.

But eight spots behind No. 5 Alabama, a team UT throttled in October?

Every single week, I'll say something to this effect: Take care of your own business and the rest takes care of itself. Tennessee offered a clear reminder of that reality, shredding No. 6 Kentucky in Week 10 and rising to eighth in Tuesday's update.

While the gap between third-ranked Bama and the No. 8 Vols is still laughable, Tennessee is nowhere near panic mode. Keep winning, and it'll be fine.

I'm not saying the CFP committee doesn't like the ACC, but I wouldn't expect a marriage proposal anytime soon.

Miami went on the road without its star receiver against a now-No. 5 Notre Dame team, clawed back within a possession and was a near-catch in the end zone from tying the game. The penalty? Fall six spots, settling one behind Texas—which has losses to a pair of 5-4 teams in Oklahoma and Florida.

Wake Forest holds an identical 8-1 record to Miami, only lost to that very Miami roster and is ranked 13th—behind five two-loss programs. SMU and Duke, which are both 7-2, couldn't crack the Top 25 over seven 6-3 teams.

I'm not saying it's indefensible. It's also worth an eye roll or three.

Saturday at noon ET, Miami hosts Duke as Wake Forest plays at SMU. Next week's update will reveal just how much the committee even considers those quality results for the winners.

Last week, the biggest loser was Notre Dame.

Thanks to a win over top-ranked Miami, however, the Fighting Irish land in the opposite category this time around. They soared to fifth in Tuesday's ranking.

An essential result in Week 10 was BYU's loss to Utah. The committee didn't have much respect for BYU's résumé, placing the Cougars ninth in the initial CFP Top 25. Without a signature win and with a loss to BYU, Notre Dame landed 11th.

Utah's win, however, meant 7-2 BYU's head-to-head victory was less impactful.

Throw in a major correction for Indiana and natural leap of Miami, and the Fighting Irish are positioned for a CFP trip if they win out.

articles.title: Hugo-Suker, protagonismo blanco el día en el que Fernando Torres entró en el Salón de la Fama de México
articles.standfirst: Los dos madridistas se roban parte del protagonismo de la gala que tuvo lugar anoche
articles.summary: Los dos madridistas se roban parte del protagonismo de la gala que tuvo lugar anoche
articles.body: MARCA fue testigo anoche del reencuentro de dos delanteros madridistas de leyenda: Hugo Sánchez y Davor Suker, que posaron para nuestra cámara pco antes del inicio de la 14ª investidura del Salón de la Fama del Fútbol de Pachuca (México), celebrada anoche en esa ciudad azteca. Hugo fue protagonista por lo siguiente. Charlyn Corral, ganadora del 'Trofeo Gerd Müller' en la pasada gala del Balón de Oro, recibió un reconocimiento especial de manos del exmadridista, que, a su vez, también recibió un homenaje por sus 50 años de carrera. Suker, por su parte, fue una de las 18 figuras del fútbol ingresadas en el Salón, junto al brasileño Bebeto; el francés Thierry Henry; el alemán Miroslav Klose; el italiano Alessandro Del Piero; y el español Fernando Torres, campeón en Sudáfrica 2010. Fernando (único español en ingresar este año) no pudo acudir al acto por sus compromisos con el filial rojiblanco. Las leyendas que homenajeadas en la categoría de 'Decanos Internacionales' fueron Teófilo Cubillas, mundialista en 1970, 1978 y 1982 y el brasileño Sócrates, quien jugó las Copas del Mundo de 1982 y 1986; falleció en el 2011. La generación 2026 de este recinto se completó con seis figuras que destacaron en el fútbol mexicano: los chilenos Fabián Estay y Humberto Suazo; los argentinos Antonio Mohamed y Christian 'Chaco' Giménez; y los mexicanos Oribe Peralta y Ramón Morales. En la categoría de 'Decanos' del fútbol nacional se premió al peruano Gerónimo Barbadillo y al mexicano Ignacio Flores. En la categoría femenina, en el plano internacional ingresó al Salón de la Fama la japonesa Homare Sawa, campeona mundial en 2011. También ingresó como parte de esta generación Mónica Vergara, ex entrenadora de la selección mexicana. El Salón de la Fama del Fútbol de Pachuca es el 'Hall of Fame' más organizado y prestigioso de todo el mundo en cuanto a este deporte. Por él, en sus 13 ediciones anteriores, han pasado los más grandes futbolistas de la historia (Maradona, Di Stéfano, Pelé...), con el único requisito de haber transcurrido cinco años desde su retirada del mundo profesional. Los miembros se eligen tras la votación de numerosos periodistas de todo el mundo (MARCA es el votante español) para la composición de los nuevos 18 miembros que son investidos en una ceremonia espectacular que cada año tiene lugar en México por estas fechas.

articles.title: College Football Playoff rankings: Georgia takes over as top Dawg; Indiana drops 5 spots on bye
articles.summary: The Georgia Bulldogs and Utah Utes sit atop this week's CFP rankings.
articles.body:
The second iteration of the College Football Playoff rankings were released on Tuesday night and there were plenty of shakeups. Last week's inaugural rankings put a no-doubt team at the top, but this week wasn't as easy.

The poll after Week 10 saw a change at the top after the Hurricanes fell to Notre Dame last week . Miami fell six spots to No. 7, and Notre Dame rose six spots to No. 5.

New No. 1 Georgia obliterated No. 19 Ole Miss to claim the top spot in the CFP rankings. This week, the Bulldogs will go on the road to face the Missouri Tigers, who have lost two of their last three games.

Two FBS teams remain unbeaten: the No. 2 Utah Utes and the No. 4 UCLA Bruins. Utah's win last week over No. 10 BYU helped the Utes move up one slot in this week's CFP rankings. This week, Utah takes on No. 23 Arizona on the road, while the Bruins will be at home against Illinois on Friday night.

The Hoosiers did not play last weekend. Yet, when the bracket was revealed on Tuesday night, Indiana's was lower expected. Last week, the Hoosiers were ranked No. 4, but this week they were ranked No. 9.

The assumption on the bracket reveal show was that Indiana's one loss — to Ohio State — looked worse after the Buckeyes lost their third game last weekend and fell in the rankings.

CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek told ESPN Indiana was "a victim of having a bye week at the wrong time" as several teams near them in the rankings earned quality wins and moved ahead of them.

Three teams Indiana beat — Northwestern, Michigan, and Minnesota — also lost last weekend. It feels like the committee overcorrected, but the Hoosiers can make up for it with a convincing win over No. 18 USC this weekend.

The Crimson Tide jumped up to No. 3 this week after being No. 7 last week. Alabama is the highest-ranked two-loss team, and is currently ranked ahead of undefeated UCLA and one-loss Notre Dame.

Alabama's two losses this season were to now-No. 1 Georgia and No. 8 Tennessee. The Crimson Tide have a tough strength of schedule, but being four spots ahead of the Volunteers, who have the head-to-head, will likely make fans confused for the second week in a row about exactly how the committee is making its decisions.

Yurachek spoke on the Alabama-Tennessee situation and said, "Alabama was in that first pool, Tennessee was not in that first pool..If you look at their schedule compared to Alabama's schedule, the committee feels like Alabama has a stronger schedule."

How could Week 11 shake up the rankings for next week?

Now that the rankings are out, we have a clearer look at this weekend's matchups.

There was hope that SMU would sneak into the top 25 to make the matchup against No. 13 Wake Forest mean a little more, but that didn't happen. Still, that game could very well determine which team Miami faces in the final ACC championship next month.

While the weekend has plenty of exciting matchups, none of them are between two teams currently projected to make the 12-team playoff.

Here is a look at the biggest matchups of the weekend with the updated ratings:

No. 7 Miami vs. Duke No. 13 Wake Forest vs. SMU No. 22 Missouri vs. No. 1 Georgia No. 18 USC vs. No. 9 Indiana No. 2 Utah vs. No. 23 Arizona No. 6 Texas vs. No. 21 LSU No. 12 Texas Tech vs. No. 25 Oklahoma State

articles.title: ‘I pay $500 for 5 square metres’: Spain’s protesters, in their own words
articles.summary: Young people are stuck in the family home or forced into cramped, overpriced rentals with little security or control.
articles.body:
Tens of thousands of young people have protested across Spain in recent weeks, rallying against the country’s acute housing crisis. On Wednesday, many have gone on strike, heeding calls by Spain’s biggest unions for a nationwide walkout under the slogan: “Salarios, vivienda y precios” – or “wages, housing, and prices”.

Anger grew last month after the forcible eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from the Madrid flat where she had lived for the past seven decades. Her corporate landlord had raised the rent to a level above her means. As the public outcry worsened, she died in hospital the day the property owners who had evicted her agreed to allow her to return to her home.

To protect vulnerable renters, the government presented two emergency decrees to parliament, but these were defeated by right-wing parties.

Spain’s left-wing coalition government called a snap election for November 29, hoping to capitalise on anger over the housing crisis to rally voters as Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez had trailed in the polls to the conservative People’s Party and the far-right Vox party.

Against this backdrop, the Bank of Spain has said the country has a shortage of 750,000 homes, but this figure could rise to 1 million by next year.

Al Jazeera spoke to several protesters about their demands:

‘I still live with my parents as housing is so expensive’

Haris Javaid Sharif, 24, a data analyst, lives with his parents, brother and sister in a 44sq-metre (474-foot) flat in Barcelona. Sharif earns $1,900 per month net. The family pay $745 for their rented flat, of which he pays half. He still lives with his parents as average rental prices for a three-bedroom flat in Barcelona range between $954 and $1,684.

“After the pandemic, we were evicted from our flat because we owed five months rent. My father and I could not work because of the pandemic. When we got the 2,500 euros ($2,800), the owner did not want to negotiate and we lost our home.

“We went 11 months without work and we lived in two-room accommodation. I thought it only happens to vulnerable people, but it can happen to anyone.

“I still live with my parents as housing is so expensive. I am joining the strike to try to press these politicians. The housing problems for youngsters is the biggest problem. I speak to people who don’t see themselves buying a house in 10 years’ time.”

‘We are worried our landlord might kick us out’

Bea Garcia de la Torre, 32, who works for a foundation in Madrid, shares a 70sq-metre (753sq-foot) flat with her brother. They pay $1,229 per month in rent. She earns $2,400 per month.

“I am not in the worst position. There are some people who have to pay half their monthly wages in rent. My brother and I share the rent, but the landlord is trying to get us to pay for the central heating, which is something which should be paid for by the community. We are also worried that he might put up the rent to an astronomical amount or kick us out.

“I will join this general strike because it is a good chance to change the housing policy in this country, just like we did with a similar action and won the right to an eight-hour day.”

‘The landlord could push up the rent or just get rid of us’

Iratxe Gonzalez, 27, a social worker, shares a flat in Madrid with three other people. She earns $1,200 per month, of which she pays $400 in rent for the flat of 45sq metres (484sq foot).

“I needed to leave my parents’ home, but the flat is very small, and we only have a short-term contract of one year. It is not very secure. The landlord could push up the rent or just get rid of us. I feel this is an issue which is important for every young person in Spain right now.”

‘The average for leaving home in Spain is 30 years old’

Ignacio Redrado, a 32-year-old teacher who could only afford to leave home when he was 26, earns $2,245 and pays $337 in rent per month. He shares a cramped flat in Madrid with four others, which measures 60 sq metres (646sq feet). They pay $1,067 per month in rent. Madrid has the highest rental prices in Spain, with an average flat for four people costing between $2,500 and $6,737.

“The average for leaving home in Spain is 30 years old. We have called a general strike because we cannot take any more. We must act. It is not about this government. The power should be with the people. We must solve the problem of housing. We want indefinite rental contracts and more social housing.”

‘My bedroom measures only two metres by 2.6 metres’

Arturo Leon, 24, works with an NGO and hopes to study for a doctorate in housing justice. He shares a small flat in Barcelona with four others and pays $506 per month in rent.

“We do not have a contract, and there are lots of things in the flat which are broken, but the landlord refuses to fix. My bedroom measures only two metres by 2.6 metres (6.6 feet by 8.5 feet). But despite this, the landlord is threatening to put up the rent. This is a perfect example of why I will be joining the general strike.”
