articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Man Utd close to agreeing deal with Michael Carrick's potential successor ahead of Monaco meeting
articles.summary: Man Utd CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are set to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe for a Monaco summit on Wednesday to review the club's start to the season; club would have to buy Mauricio Pochettino out of USA contract
articles.body:
USA boss Pochettino is being lined up as Carrick's successor with United preparing for a potential parting of ways.

Carrick reported to United's Carrington training ground on Wednesday morning at around 7.45am before it emerged that talks with Pochettino are advanced.

Sky Sports News understands United would have to pay around £7m to buy out Pochettino from his newly-signed contract with the USA but this is not thought to be an issue for the club.

Pochettino is understood to be ready if United ultimately decide to make a change at head coach, which remains likely. He is set to take charge of the USA against Haiti on Saturday as things stand.

While Carrick is in Manchester, United's powerbrokers are set to make a decision on his future at a Monaco summit on Wednesday.

CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox had already been due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe for a summit to review the club's start to the season.

But with United in the relegation zone after their worst start to a league campaign for 40 years, Carrick's future is increasingly in doubt and likely to be top of the agenda.

Berrada and Wilcox have to make their recommendation to Ratcliffe, who has control of football operations at Old Trafford, before a final decision is made over Carrick.

articles.title: El mundo de los porteros analiza el trágico choque De Miguel-Owono: "A esa velocidad no puedes frenar"
articles.standfirst: Porteros, ex porteros y formadores de guardametas analizan la jugada para MARCA
articles.summary: Porteros, ex porteros y formadores de guardametas analizan la jugada para MARCA
articles.body: Mientras se suceden los homenajes a Jesús de Miguel y el mundo del fútbol trata de digerir este duro golpe, un debate se abre paso. Como suele ocurrir en este tipo de situaciones, con una tragedia inesperada de por medio, todo es analizado al milímetro y se suelen buscar responsables, culpables o factores que pudiesen desencadenar el fatal desenlace. Pero, a veces, simplemente no los hay. La salida mal medida de Owono generará en los próximos días, como decimos, un profundo debate. Sobre esa actuación, ese gesto en concreto habitual en los porteros de atacar los balones aéreos con una rodilla al frente. Sin embargo, es todo mucho más complicado que eso. Porteros todavía en activo, exporteros, entrenadores de guardametas durante décadas.... especialistas, en definitiva, del mundo de la portería cuentan a MARCA todos los pormenores de esa jugada. Todo visto bajo el prisma de quien se enfunda unos guantes. No se trata de buscar culpables. Tampoco de añadir víctimas. Es únicamente analizar la jugada en su esencia. Para hablar de porteros en España hay que acudir, irremediablemente, a Manuel Amieiro, formador de porteros como Casillas, Diego López o Antonio Adán, entre otros, durante sus 14 años en el Real Madrid. 40 años en ese pequeño entorno que se genera entre los tres palos le avalan. Nadie mejor que él para desmenuzar la jugada: "Todas las acciones que hace el portero en situaciones de impacto son arriesgadas. Para los jugadores, pero también para el portero. Imagina que tienes que desplazarte fuera del área. Vas a mucha velocidad y, a veces, no mides bien la distancia. Tú sobre la marcha tienes que modificar el gesto de intervención", apunta. Y aquí aparece uno de los principales factores clave: EL ENTORNO. Para un portero, la acción cambia por completo si esa intervención aérea esta fuera del área. "Estás fuera de tu zona de confort, por decirlo de alguna manera. Cuando sales fuera del área te implica salir más agresivo, tienes más estrés". Es un elemento que, para Joel Robles, actual portero del CD Estoril y ex de Atlético, Everton o Betis, entre otros, no hay que pasar por alto. Sus años de experiencia en la Premier, donde el fútbol se vuelve más físico, le han hecho ver situaciones límite casi cada fin de semana: "En Inglaterra hay impactos de este estilo cada jornada. Es una situación que vas al límite. A veces es una décima de segundo, mides mal y se producen este tipo de choques. A esa velocidad no puedes frenar", lamenta el veterano guardameta. Y es ahí, al ser en esa zona, donde el gesto técnico se carga de explosividad. EL LUGAR, por tanto, juega un papel crucial. "Fuera del área intervienen muchos factores: posición inicial, distancia que haya, la capacidad para impulsarte, la velocidad que llevas... como alguno de estos aspectos vaya desajustado, se corre el riesgo de un impacto mayor o menor. Entran muchos parámetros a la hora de afrontar una situación como esta", aclara Amieiro. Dista mucho, por tanto, afrontar esa acción dentro del área a tener que afrontarlo fuera de la misma. "Ir con la rodilla arriba no implica ir fuerte. La rodilla va muchas veces sin fuerza. Pero fuera del área, atacando el balón, es diferente. Un balón bombeado dentro del área es otra cosa, pero cuando tienes que atacar el balón... No es solo por protegerte. Son situaciones aparatosas", subraya Joel Robles. Es en la enseñanza tradicional de ese gesto técnico del portero donde Óscar Medina, ex portero formado en Getafe y Atlético de Madrid e internacional sub16, incide. La FORMACIÓN se convierte en otro de los factores clave: "A nivel formativo, ese patrón de movimiento, se enseña a elevar la rodilla con el objetivo de mantener la distancia. A partir de los 5-7 años se inculca ese patrón motriz como medidad de protección. Por mucho que Owono quiera saltar con De Miguel, tenemos un portero formado que le hemos enseñado que la disputa aérea la tiene que hacer siempre con una rodilla por delante. Ya lo tiene de forma mecánica y es difícil evitarlo", apunta. Lo sabe bien otro ex portero como Sánchez Broto, que hizo carrera en el Zaragoza, Villarreal y Málaga, entre otros muchos clubes: "Desde crío te enseñaban que el portero tenía que protegerse al salir con la rodilla. La única manera de protegerte era con la rodilla. Es la forma en la que nos hacían trabajar, al menos cuando yo estaba en activo". Y es que ese habitual choque entre portero y atacante suele acabar con impactos demasiado contundentes, para ambos lados. "Yo estuve dos días en la UVI en un Lorca-Cartagena. Y fue por un choque similar. Cuando jugaba en el Pegaso estuve en el Gregorio Marañon por rotura de costillas tres noches. Me vi expuesto y salí mal parado. El portero sale así para protegerse, es inevitable", recuerda Medina. Pero el gesto técnico no se limita a una medida de protección. Hay una cuestión de FÍSICA que hacen de ese movimiento una secuencia inevitable para un portero: "No es solo por cubrirte y meter la rodilla al rival. Es por técnica. Necesitas una pierna de batida para impulsarte. La propia técnica te obliga a levantar una pierna", señala Joel Robles. "Corres, tomas impulso y el otro pie te ayuda a elevarte. Es un mecanismo natural. Es un gesto de batida para tomar impulso. Es un mecanismo que lleva ímplicito el gesto para atacar un balón aéreo. Intentamos que los niños aprendan los mecanismos básicos. Hay gente que le saca más rentabilidad y gente que vulnera lo que aprende.", corrobora Amieiro. En una acción como esta, por tanto, confluyen varios factores. El contexto juega un papel crucial. El entorno, el lugar, la velocidad a la que se produce, la formación, la toma de decisiones e incluso la física están implicadas en una situación fatal como esta. No hay consuelo, no hay justificación ni se pretende buscar para un accidente que le tocó a Jesús de Miguel, pero que se pudo dar en cualquier otro campo de fútbol. El luto continúa. También para los porteros.

articles.title: Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino: Would Argentine be the perfect fit or just another manager to fall foul of Old Trafford chaos?
articles.summary: Manchester United are close to agreeing a deal with Mauricio Pochettino if Michael Carrick is sacked; can it be third time lucky in the Premier League for the Argentine? Or is this move, as has proved with others, doomed to fail from the start?
articles.body:
Could it be that we are finally to bear witness to the culmination of this elaborate 10-year dance of incompatible circumstances?

The Old Trafford hierarchy have always admired Pochettino from afar. He was on their radar while at Tottenham and again when it was clear his time at PSG was coming to an end. The Argentine was eventually lured back to the Premier League, but instead returned to London, signing with Chelsea.

All along this journey of complicated courtship United were at play. There have been many sliding doors moments. At the time news broke of Chelsea's interest in Pochettino in 2023, United, coached by Erik ten Hag, had just been ripped to shreds by Sevilla.

The morning after that defeat all the back pages focussed on another humiliating capitulation in Europe. 'What the El was that?' one read. Another lay into the inadequacies of Harry Maguire's performance. No doubt both headlines have been recycled since. At United, the more things change, the more they stay the same.

Miraculously, it took another 18 months for the button to be pushed on Ten Hag. Four managers of varying permanency followed. Until another chance, a decade on from the first, has revealed itself to pursue the one that got away. Is this finally right place right time for Pochettino?

No doubt the 54-year-old is a coach well versed in chaos clubs. He took over at both PSG and Chelsea in times of relative instability and emerged with his reputation for making players better and creating a culture of support still in tact. Unlike any since Jose Mourinho, he is also, crucially, Premier League proven.

Originally endorsed by Sir Alex Ferguson - a fact not inconsequential despite the Scot's retirement some 13 years ago - Pochettino holds clout among football's elite. At nearly every turn of the post-Ferguson era, United have failed to appoint a leader of stature and appropriate experience, perhaps with Mourinho the only exception.

Not since the Portuguese left in 2018 have United had a coach capable of steering a ship as unyielding as this one. Admittedly the pool of figures able to captain such a vessel is small, especially one that appears to be sinking so voluntarily.

But Pochettino is a personality. On top of his attractive brand of football and a commitment to player pathways, he has proved he can handle himself under pressure, not least in his most recent role as US national head coach, at a home World Cup, where his team's campaign was overshadowed, in his own words, by "politics and manipulation".

He kept his position separate to that of President Trump's frankly scandalous attempts to undermine the competitive laws of the game. And came out the other side with a new four-year contract and a nation captivated by his character and adoptive Americanisms.

But the stop-start cadence of international management was unlikely to satisfy all of Pochettino's passions. A way back into club football at this juncture is surely advantageous for a man that has not stopped talking about his openness to a return almost since the day he left.

Now to assess the balance of risk and reward. Priced into all of his major roles has been a degree of volatility that he has been able to overcome, but unlike his most recent Premier League stint at Chelsea, the United gig requires a blind leap of faith in the middle of an already unravelling season. And comes with caveats no individual manager can be expected to apprehend.

The state of the squad and that of the wider structure of the club is hardly a compelling starting point. But perhaps that is actually part of the appeal. For all Pochettino's coaching credibility, he remains a manager without any silverware in England. He comes with a point of his own to prove, which is why joining a club close to rock bottom has its advantages. Quick wins are available.

Installing a level of respectability should buy him some time and the January window presents opportunities, too. In many ways, the redemptive element is what makes the arc mutually attractive; Pochettino is not likely to get another shot at managing a giant. However fallen. He could be the medium to long-term project coach the club needs.

Of course the soap opera element cannot be ignored. But assuming a guy who has recent experience of Trump's media storm can handle the spotlight, the real question is whether he can inspire a group of players that have already proved themselves wholly unreliable on and off the pitch this season.

Pochettino's style would at least offer a recognisable blueprint suited to the demands of the Premier League, which is more than can be said for the tactical ambiguity that exists now. And his man management skills should engender greater levels of effort and commitment, albeit he will still be saddled with the same imbalances and inefficiencies that look destined to get Michael Carrick sacked.

Objectively, that is what makes this slow burn story so fascinating. Could it work? The truth is no one really knows for sure, else Pochettino would have been handed his opportunity long before now. A position 10 years in the making. Will it be worth the wait?

articles.title: Which Section 4 football teams pull off a win at sectionals? See picks
articles.summary: Top Section 4 high school football teams vie for a sectional title and a NYS tournament berth on November 13. Take a look at which teams look the strongest.
articles.body:
Ten of Section 4's top football teams compete on November 13 for a sectional title and a run in the 2026 NYSPHSAA Football Championships. Here's a look at the matchups and which teams could take home the postseason crown.

Section 4 Class AA: Elmira (6-3) vs. Corning (6-4)

Corning and Elmira's fight for a spot at state, a now seven-year endeavor wrapped in a long-standing program rivalry, happens on November 13. Elmira, undefeated in Class AA, with a 14-8 regular-season win over Corning and home-field advantage, looks better positioned for the sectional title.

Section 4 Class A: Horseheads (8-2) vs. Union-Endicott (7-3)

Horseheads will look to avenge last season's overtime loss to Union-Endicott (21-20 OT) and, after an early regular-season win over the Tigers, will likely hand U-E the loss.

Section 4 Class B: Maine-Endwell (7-2) vs. Johnson City (8-2)

The signs all point to Maine-Endwell: an undefeated division record, including a 28-23 win over JC, an offense averaging 15 yards per reception, and a four-year sectional title streak (2021-2024). But the Wildcats have had one of the program's most successful seasons, and a key defensive performance against the Spartans (34 tackles, 6 forced fumbles, 5 fumble recoveries, and two sacks) earlier in the season shows promise regarding Johnson City's ability to pull off an upset.

Section 4 Class C: Chenango Forks (10-0) vs. Waverly (8-2)

Chenango Forks and Waverly have met in the Class C final every season since 2021 (prior to last season), and each team has two sectional titles from the four-year period. The Blue Devils won the most recent matchup (2024), 38-35. Waverly will undoubtedly give Forks a run, but the Blue Devils boast the better offense this season.

Section 4 Class D: Delhi (9-1) vs. Tioga (8-2)

Delhi handed the former state champions their first loss of the 2026 season in a dominant 41-26 win and enters the Class D final with a seven-game win streak to build on. The Bulldogs also beat Tioga 22-21 in overtime in their last Class D title matchup.

articles.title: Today’s Papers – Tresoldi top of Milan’s list, Roma in pole for Endrick
articles.summary: Good morning! Here are all today’s biggest stories from the Italian sports papers.Gazzetta dello SportMilan go for it: Tresoldi now Gerry Cardinale is pushin...
articles.body:
Good morning! Here are all today's biggest stories from the Italian sports papers.

Milan go for it: Tresoldi now Gerry Cardinale is pushing to sign Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi in January, and Ruben Amorim is considering a two-man attack with Tresoldi alongside Gonçalo Ramos. The 22-year-old is also wanted by Roberto Mancini for Italy.

Endrick, a gift for Gasp Roma are also looking for more goals, and Endrick could be the answer for Gian Piero Gasperini. "I want to play," the Brazilian says, as Real Madrid consider a loan.

Benches worth a 10 On the eve of Italy vs. France, Gazzetta compares the two coaches, Roberto Mancini and Zinedine Zidane: the strength of leaders, and of ideas.

Inter: Stones fit but under assessment, Thuram stops Inter have problems at the back and up front. John Stones has recovered from injury but is still being monitored, while Marcus Thuram has been forced to stop.

Endrick, not Milan Roma are in pole position for Endrick, and the Real Madrid forward is open to joining Gasperini. Sporting director Tony D'Amico is working to get a yes in January, and Dan Friedkin is pushing for a loan with an option to buy. Endrick, a member of the evangelical movement Athletes of Christ, has ruled out Milan, the "Devil". He has played only 141 minutes this season under José Mourinho, with one goal and one assist. "I need to grow, I'm weighing up my future," he says.

Ludi: 'Como, Paz, Endrick and the bridge with Real' Como sporting director Carlalberto Ludi discusses Nico Paz, Endrick and the club's ties with Real Madrid.

Juve torn between Sørloth and Balogun Mateo Retegui will be hard to sign, so Juventus are choosing between Alexander Sørloth and Folarin Balogun for their new striker.

Inter, Chivu loses three It isn't just Ange-Yoan Bonny who is out: Marcus Thuram and Aleksandar Stanković are also injured.

Napoli move for Cacciamani Napoli have contacted Torino about the winger.

Pio breaks records: it's a challenge to Mbappé Francesco Pio Esposito already has seven goals in 13 games for Italy, and he faces Kylian Mbappé at San Siro tomorrow. His brother Sebastiano is favourite to start on the right.

Kolo on the wing brings you a No 9 Randal Kolo Muani has impressed Luciano Spalletti as a wide player, so Juventus could sell Francisco Conceição or Edon Zhegrova to make room for a new centre-forward. As well as Sørloth and Balogun, Gianluca Scamacca is now on the list, after falling behind Nikola Krstović at Atalanta. Spalletti is also working with Under-21 coach Silvio Baldini to revive Jeff Ekhator, and Juve are speeding up the permanent deal for Guglielmo Vicario.

Torino stadium: the proposal is in Torino have presented their long-promised plan for the Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino to Turin's city council. It includes a 99-year surface-rights deal, which could help attract investors and even lead to a change of ownership at the club. Mayor Stefano Lo Russo called it a partnership project for both the stadium and the Robaldo training centre: "Finally!"

Inter fall apart again: Bonny and Thuram out Inter's attacking crisis continues. Bonny is out for a month, Thuram has left the France squad, and Stanković is also injured. Chivu is hoping for good news on Lautaro Martínez.

Tresoldi, the fan, wants Milan The Club Brugge striker, who Italy and Germany are both trying to recruit, wouldn't hesitate to join Milan. He is top of Cardinale's list, and Milan will make an attempt in January.

Twenty-two clubs for one national team Mancini's squad is drawn from 22 different clubs. Nicolò Zaniolo has gone home: "Personal reasons, it isn't easy." Alphadjo Cissè is emotional about his call-up: "Balotelli is my role model."

articles.title: Roma star reveals emotional side of Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho: “You learn so much from him”
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho has built a reputation as one of football’s most demanding managers, but there is another side to his intense personality.The Portuguese manage...
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho has built a reputation as one of football's most demanding managers, but there is another side to his intense personality.

The Portuguese manager's time at Roma may have been a mixed bag, but midfielder Niccolo Pisilli has now recalled his experiences of working under the Real Madrid coach.

In an interview with MARCA , the 22-year-old spoke about how Mourinho helped him get started in his career.

Pisilli remembers Mourinho's emotional reaction

The 22-year-old midfielder was among several academy graduates given opportunities by Mourinho during his spell in the Italian capital.

One particularly memorable moment came in December 2023, when Pisilli scored his first senior goal for Roma in a Europa League encounter against Sheriff Tiraspol.

Nicolo Pisilli established himself under Jose Mourinho. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

The youngster was overcome with emotion after scoring for his boyhood club, and his tears even moved Mourinho.

"I had to leave the dressing room because otherwise I was going to start crying too," the Portuguese manager admitted at the time.

Reflecting on their relationship, Pisilli expressed his gratitude towards Mourinho for helping him fulfil his childhood dream.

"The coach identified strongly with Roma and its atmosphere. I will always be grateful to him because he gave me the opportunity to make my debut wearing this shirt," he explained.

Roma youngster praises Mourinho's personality

Pisilli also offered an insight into Mourinho's personality away from the touchline, describing him as someone who is particularly enjoyable to work with.

"He is a very pleasant person. His career needs no introduction," the midfielder explained.

Jose Mourinho has started very well in his second stint at Real Madrid. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

"When you speak to him, you try to learn as much as possible: how he has won so much, how he has transformed so many players."

Mourinho's career took him from Roma to Fenerbahce and then Benfica before he returned to Real Madrid.

The Portuguese manager has made a brilliant start to his second spell at Real Madrid, and his team have continued to improve with every passing week .

It remains to be seen whether Mourinho can bring silverware back to the Santiago Bernabeu at the end of this campaign.
